Abstract. This document describes version 2 of the Nexora Platform API, which powers the NexaDesk, NexaFlow and
NexaInsight products. It covers the service architecture, OAuth 2.0 authentication, the main resource endpoints, request
limits by subscription plan, pagination, idempotency, webhooks and the error model. Latency objectives for each endpoint
group are given so that client teams can set timeouts correctly.
Keywords: REST API, OAuth 2.0, JWT, rate limiting, pagination, webhooks, idempotency, error codes
1. Architecture Overview
All external traffic enters through the API Gateway, which terminates TLS 1.2+, applies rate limits stored in
Redis, and routes requests to backend services running on Kubernetes (Amazon EKS). Access tokens are
verified by the Auth Service. Persistent data is stored in PostgreSQL, domain events are published to Kafka and
analytical data is stored in ClickHouse (Figure 1).
Figure 1. High-level architecture of the Nexora Platform API.
2. Base URL, Versioning and Conventions
• Base 
URL 
(production): 
https://api.nexora.example/v2; 
sandbox:
https://sandbox.api.nexora.example/v2.
• All requests and responses use JSON (UTF-8). Timestamps are ISO 8601 in UTC, for example
2026-03-01T09:30:00Z.
• Version 2 is the current version and is supported until 31 December 2027. Version 1 was retired on 30 June
2026 and returns HTTP 410 (Gone).
• Field names use snake_case. Unknown fields in requests are rejected with HTTP 422.

3. Authentication
The API uses the OAuth 2.0 client-credentials grant. A client exchanges its client_id and client_secret
for a JWT access token valid for 60 minutes. The token is then sent in the Authorization: Bearer header.
Secrets must be stored in a secrets manager and rotated at least every 90 days; they must never be committed
to source control (see Coding Standards, NX-ENG-003).
Figure 2. OAuth 2.0 client-credentials flow and token validation.
POST /v2/auth/token
Content-Type: application/json
{ "grant_type": "client_credentials",
 "client_id": "cli_8f2a91",
 "client_secret": "<stored-in-secrets-manager>",
 "scope": "tickets:read tickets:write" }
200 OK
{ "access_token": "eyJhbGciOiJSUzI1NiIs...", "token_type": "Bearer", "expires_in": 3600 }

5. Rate Limits, Pagination and Idempotency
Limits apply per API client and depend on the customer's subscription plan (see Product Documentation,
NX-PRD-001). Bursts of up to 2 times the limit are allowed for 10 seconds. Exceeding the limit returns HTTP
429 with a Retry-After header; clients should back off exponentially.
Table 2. Rate limits by subscription plan.
Plan

• Pagination: cursor-based. Use limit (default 25, maximum 100) and pass next_cursor from the
previous response.
• Idempotency: POST requests may include an Idempotency-Key; repeated requests with the same key
within 24 hours return the original response.
• Concurrency: use the If-Match header with the ticket's ETag on PATCH to avoid lost updates (HTTP 409
on conflict).
6. Webhooks
Nexora sends an HTTPS POST to registered endpoints when events such as ticket.created,
ticket.updated and workflow.completed occur. Every delivery carries an X-Nexora-Signature
header containing an HMAC-SHA256 of the raw body using the webhook secret; receivers must verify the
signature and respond with 2xx within 10 seconds. Failed deliveries are retried 5 times, after 1 minute, 5
minutes, 30 minutes, 2 hours and 12 hours.

8. Performance Objectives
Figure 3. Target p95 response latency by endpoint group (milliseconds).
Clients should set a request timeout of at least 3 times the p95 target of the endpoint group they call. Platform
availability targets are defined per subscription plan in the Product Documentation.
9. References
[1] RFC 6749: The OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework.
[2] RFC 7519: JSON Web Token (JWT).
[3] Nexora Deployment SOP, NX-ENG-002.
[4] Nexora Coding Standards, NX-ENG-003 (secrets handling).
[5] Nexora Product Documentation, NX-PRD-001 (plans and limits).
